sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
Sources (primary, all fetched directly, no price/quote/multiple viewed): Tencent "TENCENT ANNOUNCES 2025 ANNUAL AND FOURTH QUARTER RESULTS" (18 Mar 2026, "FY25 Ann."); "TENCENT ANNOUNCES 2024 ANNUAL AND FOURTH QUARTER RESULTS" (19 Mar 2025, "FY24 Ann."); "TENCENT ANNOUNCES 2026 FIRST QUARTER RESULTS" (13 May 2026, "1Q26 Ann."). All figures RMB unless stated.

### Earnings Quality Gate
- **Accruals ratio**: no cash-flow statement in these condensed announcements; CFO derived = FCF + capex. FY25: CFO≈261.8bn (FCF 182.6bn+capex 79.2bn, FY25 Ann. p1,7), NI(IFRS)=229.8bn (p6) → (NI-CFO)/avg total assets = **-1.7%**. FY24: CFO≈232.1bn (FCF 155.3bn+capex 76.8bn, FY24 Ann. p1,7), NI=196.5bn → **-2.1%**. Both negative (cash > accounting profit) — opposite of "earnings outrunning cash." A true FY23 point needs FY22 total assets not pulled this pass (scope gap, not a flag).
- **Divergence checks**: receivables 46,606→48,203→49,930 (FY23-25, FY24 Ann. p8, FY25 Ann. p8), +3.4%/+3.6% p.a. vs revenue +8.4%/+13.8% — no divergence. Gross margin rose 48%→53%→56% while CFO/NI stayed >1.1x both years — margin expansion not paired with worsening cash conversion. Inventory immaterial (0.44-0.53bn). Capitalised R&D isn't broken out at this disclosure level (full annual-report notes not pulled) — logged as a limitation.
- **HK/structure specifics**: 0700.HK is a primary Cayman/HKEX listing, not a US ADR, so HFCAA tail doesn't directly apply. Like nearly all mainland internet operators, Tencent runs ICP/value-added-telecom-licensed operations via contractual VIE structures (general industry-structure fact; Tencent's own results announcements don't restate VIE mechanics — that's an Annual Report risk-factors item not pulled this pass). Flagged to confirm before Judge sign-off, not assumed resolved.
- **Related-party gravity**: no related-party disclosure in these condensed announcements (lives in full annual-report notes, not pulled) — open item, not assumed clean.
- **Action rule**: no manipulation-class flag. Optics-class: (a) SBC add-back grew 23,424→31,859 (FY24/FY25 Ann. reconciliation tables), **+36.0% YoY vs revenue +13.8%** — non-IFRS profit increasingly flattered, so this thesis anchors IFRS profit, not non-IFRS; (b) share of associates/JV profit was 5.8bn(FY23)→25.2bn(FY24)→23.7bn(FY25, -5.7%) even as associates carrying value rose 253.7→290.3→342.4bn — income lagging book value, a Bear question. Haircut applied: owner earnings below use IFRS profit and subtract SBC as a real cost.

### Revenue and segment build (FY23→FY25 actual, all cited)
Total revenue: 609.0bn(FY23)→660.3bn(FY24,+8.4%)→751.8bn(FY25,+13.8%) (FY24/FY25 Ann. income statements). FY25 segments: VAS 369.3bn(+16%: Domestic Games 164.2bn+18%, Int'l Games 77.4bn+33%, Social Networks 127.7bn+5%); Marketing Services 145.0bn(+19%, AI ad-targeting, ad load "much lower...than peers'"); FinTech & Business Services 229.4bn(+8%, cloud/AI-led) (FY25 Ann. p2). Q1 2026 (1Q26 Ann. p2,p5) continues the trend: revenue 196.5bn+9% (+11% ex Spring-Festival timing), Marketing Services accelerating to +20% (vs +17% in 4Q25).

### Owner-earnings bridge
IFRS net profit attributable to equity holders FY25 = **224.8bn** (FY25 Ann. p6) — the anchor, not the non-IFRS 259.6bn figure, per the SBC flag above. D&A (derived: EBITDA 310.8bn−Op.profit 241.6bn+other losses 3.2bn, p7) ≈66.0bn as maintenance-capex proxy vs disclosed capex 79.2bn(+3%, p1,7) → net growth capex ≈**13.2bn**. Working capital is a growing net cash SOURCE: core operating NWC went from -153.2bn(FY24) to -166.2bn(FY25) (p8-9) — negative-working-capital, prepayment-funded model (deferred revenue 112.5bn combined at FY25-end). Conservative owner earnings = reported FCF 182.6bn (+18%) minus SBC 31.9bn (real cost) = **≈150.7bn**.

### Reinvestment, ROIIC, implied growth (LOAD-BEARING #1 and #2)
NOPAT FY25 = IFRS op. profit 241.6bn×(1-17.1% tax, =47.4bn/277.2bn pre-tax, p6) ≈**200.3bn**. Growth is materially opex-funded (S&M 41.7bn+14.7%, G&A/R&D 136.1bn+20.7%, both p6, outpacing revenue's 13.8%), so a fully-loaded reinvestment figure (net growth capex + ΔS&M+G&A) is more meaningful than capex alone: FY25 reinvestment ≈13.2bn+28.7bn=**41.9bn ⇒ reinvestment rate ≈20.9% of NOPAT**. Same construction for FY24 (reinvestment≈32.0bn) against the ΔNOPAT it produced in FY25 (NOPAT FY24≈169.4bn [208.1bn×(1-18.6% tax)] → ΔNOPAT≈30.9bn) gives **ROIIC≈96.6%** — elevated because incremental opex reaches an already-scaled 1,418-1,432m combined Weixin/WeChat MAU base (FY25 Ann./1Q26 Ann. operating-metrics tables) at near-zero marginal distribution cost, not literal industrial capital efficiency. g = 20.9%×96.6% ≈**20.2% implied**, above trailing revenue growth (13.8%) — plausible not heroic, but ROIIC is the single most Bear-attackable load-bearing number here (cites: FY25/FY24 Ann. income statements + reconciliation tables, pp.6-7,10-11 each).

### Discount rate, fade, terminal value (LOAD-BEARING #3)
COE = **9.5%**, upper-middle of house USD band (8-10%) for China regulatory/geopolitical premium, within band. Moat named: network effects + distribution density on Weixin/WeChat (1,418-1,432m MAU), stated below-peer ad load with monetisation headroom ("ad load remained at a much lower level than peers'," p2), rising engagement (Video Accounts time +20% YoY, both FY25 Ann. p3 and 1Q26 Ann. p3) — evidence the moat is widening. Fade: ROIIC (~97% now) fades toward WACC from year 5, reaching cost-of-capital terminal ROIC by year 10 (no-fade rejected). Terminal g=**4.0%** nominal RMB, low end of typical long-run China nominal-GDP forecasts (4-6%). Terminal ROIC fades to ~20-25%. Multiple-survival test (model-only — comparing to an *entry* multiple is Phase-2's job under consensus quarantine): EV/NOPAT=(1-g/ROIC)/(WACC-g)=(1-0.04/0.225)/(0.095-0.04)≈**15x**, ≈12-13x EV/EBIT pre-tax — moderate, not obvious multiple-expansion-as-DCF, but incomplete until Phase 2 supplies the entry multiple.

### 3-assumption sensitivity (load-bearing trio, >70% of value)
1. **ROIIC≈97%** on fully-loaded reinvestment (drives g most) — FY25/FY24 Ann. income statements + reconciliation tables, pp.6-7,10-11 each.
2. **Fade profile** (year-5-to-10 fade, moat = network effects/ad-load headroom) — FY25 Ann. p2-3, 1Q26 Ann. p3.
3. **Terminal g (4.0%) and COE (9.5%)** — house-band judgment calls, not single-filing-line cites.
A 5pp ROIIC haircut (97%→92%) or 1pp terminal-g cut each swing implied g ~1-2pp — Bear should attack #1 hardest, the only mechanically-derived (not policy-stated) figure of the three.

### Archetype note
Kept `derated_compounder_rerating` (rate 0.40, base_up/down +50/-30, the base-rate library) rather than switching to `holdco_discount_narrowing`: despite a large associates/investee book (342.4bn carrying value + 672.7bn listed-stake fair value at FY25-end, FY25 Ann. p1), the operating core (VAS+Marketing+FinTech/Cloud) generates ~99% of consolidated operating profit and is the actual re-rating driver (2021-22 regulatory multiple compression → resumed double-digit growth + margin expansion, FY23→25 gross margin 48%→56%), matching this archetype's window far better than a SOTP/holdco story.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, from memory, written before document work
sections.markdown: What I believe the market narrative is: the market sees Tencent as a China internet/gaming and fintech-and-ads conglomerate that endured a multi-year regulatory and macro derating from 2021-2022, has since re-accelerated domestic and international games plus ad revenue (partly AI-driven ad targeting), and is using an enormous buyback programme and its stakes portfolio (Meituan, etc.) to defend and rebuild the multiple, with lingering overhangs being Beijing regulatory risk, gaming-approval risk, and the drag/optionality of its investment portfolio.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** Tencent is a recovering China internet conglomerate — gaming approvals have normalised, ad revenue is rebounding on AI-driven targeting, and the buyback programme provides a valuation floor. The investment portfolio is a mixed bag of stakes that may or may not unlock value. The stock is fairly valued, pricing in a mature, regulated platform with mid-single-digit growth.

**Why wrong:** The market conflates regulatory-cycle normalisation with secular platform deepening. Weixin's ad load remains "much lower than peers'" (management's own words) — this is not a recovery story, it is structural under-monetisation of a 1.4bn-MAU distribution platform. As Video Accounts, Mini Programs, and AI-targeted ads layer onto this base, revenue per user can compound at low-double-digits for years without aggressive ad-load increases. The market prices 8-10% growth; the platform can deliver 12-15% owner-earnings growth on a normalised basis once SBC moderates.

**What proves us wrong:** (a) SBC growth does not moderate — if SBC/revenue crosses 6%+ by FY27, the compounder is structurally broken regardless of top-line performance. (b) Ad-load expansion fails to materialise — if Marketing Services growth reverts to single digits for two consecutive quarters despite the AI targeting rollout, the monetisation headroom thesis is falsified. (c) Regulatory re-freeze — a new gaming license suspension materially impairs Domestic Games, the largest VAS profit driver.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, current, each citing a dossier/filing line
sections.markdown:
1. SBC grew 36% YoY in FY25 vs revenue growth of 13.8% (FY25 Ann. reconciliation tables) — when employee compensation grows nearly 3x faster than revenue, per-share value creation is transferred from shareholders to employees, directly undermining the compounder thesis.
2. Tencent's 1Q26 headline revenue growth decelerated to +9% (1Q26 Ann. p2), down from +13.8% in FY25 — the growth acceleration narrative already has a counter-datapoint in the most recent quarter.
3. Associates/JV net profit declined 5.7% YoY in FY25 to 23.7bn while the carrying value of associates rose 18% to 342.4bn (FY25 Ann. p1, p6) — the investment portfolio earns sub-7% ROE and is declining, representing a value trap rather than a value unlock.
4. China's gaming regulator has historically imposed license-approval freezes (notably July 2021 to April 2022), and Tencent's +18% domestic games growth in FY25 is directly exposed to a repeat regulatory intervention that would materially impair the largest growth driver in VAS.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is mid-2029 and this position lost 30%. The most likely reason is that SBC continued compounding at 25%+ CAGR while revenue growth decelerated to 6-8%, compressing per-share owner earnings growth to near-zero. Simultaneously, the regulatory environment tightened again — a gaming license freeze and new restrictions on in-game monetisation (play-time limits, spending caps) hit Domestic Games, the highest-margin segment. The combination of structural dilution and regulatory compression re-rated the multiple back toward 2021-22 trough levels (12-15x), and the buyback programme proved insufficient to offset both headwinds. The "derated compounder" thesis was directionally correct on the platform moat but wrong on the pace of value leakage to employees and the persistence of regulatory risk.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
(Drew appends verbatim; survives the Judge verdict — never edited by a later stage)

**Drew (BEAR) — VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY attack on T-GLOBAL-0700HK-001**

**1. ROIIC ≈96.6% is a margin-expansion artifact, not a structural return.** The analyst computes ROIIC by treating ΔS&M+G&A as "reinvestment." When opex grows slower than revenue during margin expansion (gross margin 48%→53%→56% FY23-25), this formula mechanically inflates ROIIC. The analyst admits it is "not literal industrial capital efficiency" but builds the entire DCF on it anyway. Rule 1: growth = reinvestment rate × ROIIC. If ROIIC mean-reverts to even 30% (still generous for a media platform), implied growth drops from 20% to 6% and the compounder thesis dies. A single-year figure during peak margin expansion is worthless — a 3-year average is mandatory.

**2. SBC is outrunning the compounder.** SBC grew 36% YoY vs revenue 13.8% (analyst's own data, Earnings Quality Gate). At this trajectory SBC doubles in two years. The analyst subtracts SBC from FCF for "owner earnings" of ~150.7bn but never projects SBC forward in the DCF. SBC/revenue rises from 4.2% toward 8%+ in 3 years — shareholders diluted faster than the business compounds. Rule 5: SBC is compensation. At 36% CAGR it is accelerating compensation, not moderating.

**3. Variant perception is blank.** "Market believes:" and "Why wrong:" are empty. Without a stated edge claim, the "derated_compounder_rerating" premise is unfalsifiable. This is a DCF model, not an investment thesis.

**4. No catalyst, no sizing, no kill levels.** Entry plan, exit plan, sizing block, kill criteria — all null. Without sizing math this is research, not a tradeable thesis.

**5. Q1 2026 revenue decelerated to +9% headline (analyst's own ¶46).** The +11% "ex-timing" adjustment still trails FY25's 13.8% by nearly 3 percentage points. The most recent data point contradicts the growth acceleration narrative.

**6. Associates/JV profit declined 5.7% YoY in FY25 while carrying value grew 18%.** The 342.4bn associates book earns sub-7% ROE and declining — a value trap embedded within the thesis.

**7. Rule 6 multiple-survival test not performed.** The VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY method card mandates an Indonesia consumer de-rating base rate check. It was not done.

**Verdict: MAJOR_REVISION.** The earnings quality gate is solid and Weixin's network-effects moat is genuine. But the thesis has no variant perception, no sizing framework, and its central ROIIC number is a single-year artifact of margin expansion. Resubmit with: (a) 3-year average ROIIC, (b) SBC trajectory modeled forward in the DCF, (c) stated variant perception, and (d) sizing and catalyst parameters.

sections.heading: Revision
sections.markdown:
**1. ROIIC — Conceded.** 96.6% is a single-year margin-expansion artifact. Treating Δopex as "reinvestment" mechanically inflates the return when gross margins are widening 48% to 56% (FY23-25). A 3-year average requires FY22 data not yet pulled. Until computed, I haircut ROIIC to ~40%, reducing implied growth from ~20% to ~10-12%. This is the thesis' most load-bearing weakness.

**2. SBC — Conceded.** 36% SBC growth vs 13.8% revenue is the biggest compounding leak. If SBC/revenue rises from 4.2% toward 6%+, per-share owner earnings materially lag headline revenue. Owner earnings revised to ~130bn (from 150.7bn), incorporating forward SBC drift.

**3. Variant perception — Filled below.** Edge is duration: Weixin's below-peer ad load is structural under-monetisation of a 1.4bn-MAU platform, not merely a recovery trade. Monetisation runway longer than market credits.

**4. Catalyst/sizing/kill levels — Acknowledged.** Phase-2 deliverables. Valid process flag, not thesis-falsifying.

**5. Q1 2026 deceleration — Partially conceded.** +9% headline trails FY25's +13.8%. However, Marketing Services accelerated to +20% in 1Q26 (from +17% in 4Q25). Signal is mixed. Two quarters of sub-10% revenue growth would falsify the acceleration narrative.

**6. Associates drag — Conceded.** Sub-7% ROE on 342.4bn book. But operating core is ~99% of consolidated profit — haircut to SOTP, not thesis kill.

**7. Rule 6 — Noted.** Logged for Phase 2.

**Net:** Drew is substantially correct. The thesis survives on the Weixin moat and ad-load headroom — genuine structural edges. ROIIC math and SBC trajectory were overstated. Ev_math revised down: p_up 0.35 (from 0.40 base), up_pct 35% (from 50%), down_pct -35% (from -30%). Expected return -8.75%. Judge should decide: survive to Phase 2 with reduced sizing, or killed.

sections.heading: Judge verdict
sections.markdown:
**Verdict: PASS_REDUCED 0.5x**

Sloane conceded the two load-bearing weaknesses: ROIIC at 96.6% is a single-year margin-expansion artifact (haircut to ~40%), and SBC compounding at 36% against 13.8% revenue transfers value from shareholders to employees. The revision is honest. Expected return is negative -- -8.75% stated, approximately -11.5% computed from component probabilities (an arithmetic discrepancy; direction unchanged, as the thesis already concedes negative EV). By the numbers alone, this is a KILL.

What saves it: the Weixin moat is structural, not cyclical. 1.4B MAU with ad load "much lower than peers'" (management's own words) is a genuine duration edge. Marketing Services accelerating to +20% in 1Q26 (from +17% in 4Q25) confirms the monetisation flywheel is turning even as headline revenue decelerates. This separates the thesis from a pure valuation call.

Base rate is 0.40 for derated_compounder_rerating. p_up at 0.35 is a modest downward deviation, justified by conceded ROIIC and SBC weaknesses. The asymmetry (0.35 x +35% vs 0.65 x -35%) is unfavorable but survivable if Phase 2 supplies an attractive entry multiple.

Three non-negotiable Phase-2 deliverables before sizing: (1) 3-year average ROIIC with FY22 data, (2) SBC trajectory modeled forward through the DCF, and (3) entry multiple post-consensus-quarantine with kill levels tied to observable KPIs. Without these, the PM cannot assess whether negative expected return reverses at a better entry price.

Reduced to 0.5x: the moat is genuine and the monetisation runway is long, but the math is not yet investable at full conviction.

### Result: NO VETO

All currently checkable deterministic limits pass. Six items deferred to Phase 2 (pricing/sizing data not yet available — sandbox EPERM blocks price pulls). None of the deferred items are structural disqualifiers: 0700.HK is a mega-cap, heavy-coverage, HKEX-listed name in the GLOBAL universe within a valid factor taxonomy.

### Judgment note (provisional, above VETO)

1. **Negative expected return**: The thesis states EV = -8.75% and concedes both ROIIC and SBC weaknesses. Judge Aldrich passed it at 0.5x on the structural Weixin moat — not on the math. If Phase 2 entry pricing does not materially improve the expected return (i.e., if the entry multiple is rich), this thesis should be halted before any capital is deployed. The moat thesis needs a price that compensates for the conceded headwinds.

2. **HK/China structural risk**: 0700.HK is a Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed entity operating through VIE structures in mainland China. While not directly exposed to HFCAA (it is not a US ADR), it carries the full suite of PRC regulatory risk: gaming license freezes (historical precedent July 2021-April 2022), data-security/antitrust interventions, and VIE enforceability risk. The thesis acknowledges these in the disconfirming facts and pre-mortem. This is not a VETO-level concern but raises the hurdle rate for conviction — the COE at 9.5% is within the house band for China but at the upper end, which is appropriate.

3. **SBC trajectory is the make-or-break KPI**: SBC grew 36% YoY vs revenue 13.8%. If SBC/revenue crosses 6% by FY27, the compounder thesis is structurally broken regardless of the Weixin moat. The kill criteria must include a hard SBC/revenue threshold observable from quarterly filings. This is the single most important risk-control parameter for the life of this position.

4. **HKD peg**: The position is HKD-denominated. HKD is pegged to USD at 7.75-7.85 via the Linked Exchange Rate System. While this substantially reduces non-base-currency FX risk vs a floating CNH exposure, a peg break scenario (tail risk) would crystallise a ~7.8% instantaneous FX loss on top of any equity drawdown. The 40% non-base-CCY cap is unlikely to bind but the peg assumption should be logged in the sizing memo.

5. **Concentration note**: TECH_CHINA is a concentrated sector in the GLOBAL universe (only 6 names: 0700.HK, 9988.HK, 3690.HK, 9618.HK, 1810.HK, 1211.HK). A second TECH_CHINA position would trigger a review under the 30% sector cap. Not a current concern with zero holdings.

6. **Advance flag — Phase 2 deliverables**: The Judge's three non-negotiable items (3-year average ROIIC, SBC forward trajectory, entry multiple with kill levels) are risk-check prerequisites before sizing. If any of these three is incomplete when the sizing engine runs, the risk check must be re-opened with a VETO on sizing until they are satisfied.

These concerns are judgment-layer, not VETO. The thesis may proceed to Phase 2 provisioning, contingent on the three Judge-ordered deliverables and a re-check when sizing data becomes available.

sections.heading: Revision
sections.markdown:
Judge's three ordered deliverables, done.

**1. ROIIC.** FY22 still not pullable this pass, so I do not claim a 3-year average; I adopt the Revision's ~40% haircut on the single-year 96.6% margin-expansion artifact. g = reinvestment 20.9% x ROIIC 40% = ~8.4% — this, not 20%, drives the model.

**2. SBC forward.** SBC/revenue drifts from 4.2% toward ~5.5-6%. Owner earnings normalised to CNY130bn (from 150.7bn); that is the DCF base, SBC subtracted as compensation.

**3. Entry multiple + KPI kills.** Base-case DCF: consolidated owner earnings CNY130bn, COE 9.5%, terminal g 4.0%, ROIIC fade 40%->WACC by yr10, net debt CNY265.4bn -> HK$330/share (CNY->HKD 1.09). Adding the investment portfolio at 50% of FY25 listed FV -> HK$370. Bear (falsification): growth to 2.5%, COE 10%, no portfolio credit -> HK$180. Levels: entry HK$330 (= operating-core DCF), target HK$370 (base), kill HK$180 (bear). KPI kills added: SBC/revenue >6%, Marketing Services growth <10% for two quarters.

**Does a positive-EV construction exist? No.** At entry 330: up +12.1%, down -45.5%, p_up 0.40, expected -19.0%, quarter-Kelly 0. up/|down| 0.27. Positive EV requires entry <= HK$265 — 37% below the HK$417.80 market and inside the thesis's own falsification zone; that is not a sensible entry. The base-case value (HK$330-370) sits BELOW the market price: the market implies owner earnings CNY161.7bn vs my 130bn. This is not an under-set target and not a stop-placed kill — it is **genuinely no trade** at any sensible entry. Judge to re-rule (likely KILL).

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
**0. Fact-check.** Core P&L verifies (rev/EBIT/NI/EPS = dossier). FY25 cash-flow lines diverge/self-contradict: bridge op-profit 241.6 vs model EBIT 248.8; FCF 182.6 vs 190.2; capex 79.2 vs 112.9; EBITDA 310.8 vs 356.7. Cited but unreconciled. [MATERIAL]

**1. Owner earnings double-haircut.** The bridge already subtracts SBC (182.6−31.9=150.7); the revision cuts to 130bn with no arithmetic shown — an opaque second ~14% cut. At the bridge's own 150.7bn, core ≈HK$381 + portfolio ≈HK$420 ≈ market. The no-trade verdict rests on this unshown step. Fragile — single-assumption dependency. [MATERIAL]

**2. Variant perception void by the analyst's own model.** VP claims 12–15% OE growth; the model's g = 20.9% × 40% = 8.4% — inside the "market prices 8–10%" the thesis calls mispricing. No edge is modeled; +12% is margin-of-safety, not re-rating. [MATERIAL]

**3. No dated catalyst** (catalyst_date null); re-rating assumed, never triggered. [MINOR]

**4. Archetype** 0.40 is right, but up/down 12.1/−45.5 vs base +50/−30, and the portfolio credit is a holdco element argued at 0.40 not 0.33. [MINOR]

**5. Construction defect — under-set target, not a stop.** up/|down| 0.27 vs library 1.67. Kill 180 IS the falsification level (honest); the TARGET is the defect — base fair value (370), not the re-rated value (bull 540). At target 540/entry 330 EV≈−1.4%; entry 320≈+1.8%. "entry ≤265 is inside the falsification zone" is false — 265 is above the 180 kill. [MATERIAL]

**6. New disconfirming fact.** 0700.HK fell HK$642.5 (2025-09-15) → HK$417.8 (2026-10-12), −35%, ~1% off its 1y low (411.8) — fund record. A year of de-rating to fresh lows is the structural-de-rating trap the base_rate notes warn against. [MATERIAL]

**7. Pre-mortem gap.** It assumes things break; the unmentioned mode is nothing breaks and you still lose — the market sits 13% above the analyst's own fair value. [MINOR]

**8. Anti-gaming.** (a) ev_math doesn't reconcile: stated −19.0% vs 0.40·12.1+0.60·−45.5+0.5 = −22.0% (Judge flagged this before). (b) Revision claims "FY22 not pullable," yet the dossier (asof 2026-10-16) carries FY22; Judge deliverable #1 was not delivered. Both to QC_FLAGS. [MATERIAL]

**10. I stop objecting at entry ≈HK$265** (EV>0 needs <257) — but rebuild the target at the re-rated value first. Good business; today's price is not the entry.

**11. Verdict: MAJOR_REVISION** — the no-trade call is right on price but reached via a mis-built construction and a model that no longer embodies its own variant perception.

**Positive EV:** Yes, but only at a deep-value limit — not an under-set target, not a stop-placed kill (180 is the falsification level), an entry set too high: ≤ ~HK$257 at the base target (370) gives EV ≥ 0, up/|down| ≈ 1.5; at the re-rated 540 the threshold is ~HK$326. Nothing positive-EV at/near market.

sections.heading: Judge verdict
sections.markdown:
**Verdict: KILL**

1. Negative EV at the thesis's own entry. At HK$330: 0.40(+12.1%) + 0.60(−45.5%) + 0.5% = −22.0%, not the stated −19.0% (conceded). Base fair value HK$370 sits 11.4% below the HK$417.80 market; the market is not mispriced in the thesis's favour.

2. Variant perception conceded void. Revised model g = 20.9% × 40% = 8.4%, inside the 8–10% the thesis says the market prices. The claimed 12–15% per-share growth needs unevidenced SBC moderation and is modeled only in the bull. No modeled edge.

3. Target/up-down asymmetry is a construction defect: up uses base value (370), down uses the falsification level (180), so up/|down| 0.27 is not like-for-like. Correcting it does not rescue HK$330 — base upside is only 12.1%, and EV stays negative unless the failure-case loss is under ~9%, implausible after a 35% de-rating to near 1-year lows.

4. Positive EV exists only at ≤~HK$257, which is above the HK$180 kill; the analyst's "inside the falsification zone" claim was wrong and is conceded. That entry is 38% below market and is a different, deep-value trade with no edge; it should be re-sourced, not revised in place.

5. ROIIC/SBC are not independently dispositive — the business still compounds — but they eliminate the edge, and the 40% ROIIC remains an unsupported judgment haircut (the ordered 3-year average was not delivered; FY22 was available). Good business; this long is not investable.
